newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OMB's Raines sees good chance for budget deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OMB's Raines sees good chance for budget deal.

text.p: Office of Management and Budget director Frank Raines said Wednesday he saw a good opportunity to reach a balanced budget agreement this year.

Raines, speaking to the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, cited comments by congressional leaders on their willingness to reach a budget deal, improvements in the deficit in the past four years and a good economic situation as reasons for his optimism.

"I think we have conditions in place where we can in fact move to a balanced budget by agreeing on policies that will get us there," he said. "There has been renewed emphasis on bipartisanship, on working together," Raines added.

President Clinton's new director of budget policy, Raines said he has little faith in attempts to achieve a balanced budget by regulatory enforcement. "I don't believe you can regulate your way to a balanced budget," he said.

While agreement on budget forecasting methods and accounting, and methods to enforce budget deals can help reach an agreement, they cannot force Congress and the White House to make the decisions needed to reduce the deficit, he said.
"What will balance the budget is agreement by policymakers to do so," he added.
